Instructions to candidates:

- Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.
- Question ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.
- Each question that is sub-divided has the sub marks in brackets.
- In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.
- If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.
- NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

questions.enonce_markdown:
4. (a) State TWO Assumptions made by Von Thünen in his Agricultural Land use theory.

[2 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
Johann Heinrich von Thünen (a German landowner, 1826) explained the pattern of farming round a town with a model based on assumptions. Two of them:

1. **The area is an isolated state with one central town (market)** that buys all the farm produce, and there is no outside trade.
2. **The land is a flat, uniform plain** with the same soil, climate and fertility everywhere, and no rivers or hills.

(Other assumptions: transport is by horse and cart and the cost rises with distance; farmers are rational and want to make the highest profit; the prices of produce are the same in the market.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Describe TWO problems caused by Agricultural activities on the environment.

[4 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Soil erosion and soil degradation.** Clearing forest for farmland, over-cultivation and over-grazing leave the soil bare. Rain and wind carry the fertile top soil away, gullies form, and the land becomes poor, which can lead to desertification in dry areas. Clearing forests also destroys wildlife habitats and reduces biodiversity.
2. **Pollution.** Chemical fertilisers and pesticides are washed from the fields into rivers and lakes, which pollutes the water, kills fish and causes eutrophication (a rapid growth of algae that uses up the oxygen). Burning of bush and the methane from cattle and rice fields add gases to the atmosphere and help global warming.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Outline FOUR strategies used by Newly Industrialized Countries (NICs) to experience rapid economic growth.

[4 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
Newly Industrialised Countries (for example South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Hong Kong, Brazil and Mexico) grew quickly by the following strategies:

1. **Export-oriented industrialisation:** they made manufactured goods (textiles, electronics, cars) for the world market and earned foreign exchange.
2. **Attracting foreign investment:** they gave tax holidays, set up export processing zones and welcomed transnational companies, which brought capital, technology and jobs.
3. **Cheap, disciplined and increasingly skilled labour, with investment in education:** low wages kept costs down and schools and technical training raised skills.
4. **Strong government planning and good infrastructure:** the state built ports, roads, railways and power stations, protected young industries at first and encouraged saving and investment.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) Name any THREE Multipurpose River Development Projects.

(ii) Select one of the projects and, state THREE reasons why it was carried out.

[6 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Three multipurpose river projects:** the Tennessee Valley Authority (USA); the Aswan High Dam on the Nile (Egypt); the Volta River Project at Akosombo (Ghana). (Others: Kariba on the Zambezi, the Lagdo dam on the Benue in Cameroon, the Damodar Valley in India.)

**(ii) The Aswan High Dam (Egypt), built on the Nile in the 1960s, which formed Lake Nasser.** Three reasons why it was carried out:

1. **Flood control:** before the dam the Nile flooded in some years and was very low in others; the dam stores the flood water and controls the flow.
2. **Generating hydroelectricity:** the power station supplies electricity to cities and industries.
3. **Irrigation:** water stored in Lake Nasser allows farmers to irrigate all the year, to grow more than one crop a year and to bring new land into use.

(Other reasons: water for drinking, fishing in the lake, improved river navigation, tourism.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(e) Give FOUR reasons why tourism is an important economic activity.

[4 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **It earns foreign exchange** from the money spent by visitors on hotels, food, guides and souvenirs.
2. **It creates employment**, directly (hotels, guides, drivers, park staff) and indirectly (farmers, craftsmen and traders who supply the tourists).
3. **It encourages the development of infrastructure** such as roads, airports, electricity, water supply and communications, which also help local people.
4. **It brings income to the government and to local communities** through taxes, park fees and licences, and helps the development of backward regions through the multiplier effect.

(Other reasons: it encourages the protection of wildlife and the environment, and the preservation of local culture and crafts.)
